newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks closer lower as selling hits banks.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks closer lower as selling hits banks.

text.p: Australian shares slipped more than one percent on Monday as investors factored in the effects of a possible U.S. rate increase on local bonds, taking some of the gloss off the high yielding bank sector.

The benchmark All Ordinaries index ended 28.7 points lower at 2,421.1, but off its intra-session low of 2,413.7. The March share price index futures contract finished down 34 points at 2,393, a 28.1 point discount to the underlying index.
Dealers said the steep fall indicated that investors had decided to err on the side of caution after negative comments from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan last week.
All of Australia's major banks, which have a heavy weighting in the All Ordinaries, finished weaker on solid volume.
"The big banks have been hot for a long time now. It's easy for investors to decide to take some profit in the interim," a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage said.
However, the dealer said that once the U.S. market had settled down, it was likely that investors would buy back into the major banks.
"Banks still offer the double inducement of comparatively high yields and the prospect of takeover activity after the Wallis enquiry is handed down," the dealer said.
The Wallis inquiry into Australia's financial system, due to be released at the end of March, is widely expected to recommend that mergers between Australia's biggest banks be allowed.

The two big banks worst affected by selling were Commonwealth Bank of Australia, whose shares closed 24 cents lower at A$12.58 (US$9.81), and Australia and New Zealand Banking Group which dropped 25 cents to A$7.79.

The resource sector was also bruised by selling with heavyweights CRA Ltd and The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) dropping on sizeable volume. CRA shares fell 49.2 cents to A$18.80 and BHP dropped 27 cents to A$16.78.
The reporting season continued in earnest with a mixed bag of results from a swag of medium sized companies.

Insurance group HIH Winterthur's shares ended three cents firmer at A$3.12 after it announced a full year net profit of A$61.5 million. The insurer said it expected considerable premium growth in calendar 1997.

Shares of Papua New Guinea oil producer Oil Search closed down 10 cents at A$2.55 after its year net profit rose slightly to A$24.05 million. Horticultural group Arthur Yates ended steady after posting a half net profit of A$4.2 million, down 6.9 percent on the previous corresponding half.
The shares of Adelaide-based pharmaceutical company, F.H. Faulding and Co closed lower despite a 30.7 percent rise in the group's half year net profit to A$16.21 million.

Sydney Harbour Casino announced an 18 month net loss of A$4.82 million while Papua New Guinea (PNG) gold miner, Niugini Mining recorded a year loss of A$38.91 million compared to a profit of A$5.02 million in 1995.

Bucking the negative trend was Bougainville Copper, which closed two cents higher at 58 cents after the PNG government said on Sunday that it wanted to buy CRA's controlling stake in Bougainville's closed Panguna copper mine.
